title: Commander Anthology Volume II: card flavor text

paragraphs.text: Ask your query and be on your way. Just don't look her in the eye.
As Glissa searches for the truth about Memnarch, Bosh searches to unearth the secrets of his past.
"She will come back to me."
"Now the scaled ones rule Tarkir."
"Through me, the Great Teacher's voice will rattle this world."
The fastest way across the dunes is above.
Though giants are mortal, they live so long and on such a grand scale that many small folk don't believe they ever truly die.
Enduring the most desolate and dangerous conditions, Abzan sentries unfailingly guard the stronghold gates.
Avacyn's holy warriors kept hope alive in her darkest hours. Now they will carry that hope across Innistrad.
"What we knew as Emeria, Ula, and Cosi were not divine beings at all, but a cruel trick, and a grave error." —*The Invokers' Tales*
The best techniques outlive their creators.
Light's champion in the stronghold of darkness.
The Orzhov care not for repentance, only repayment.
Exhale, and let the winds carry your soul for all eternity.
A blazing sun that never sets.
The corruption stirred the heavens above, awaking a shining champion.
Its graceful glide paints the ocean floor with strokes of luminescence.
"You are beneath contempt. Your lineage will be forgotten."
"Her voice is insight, piercing and true." —Ixidor, reality sculptor
"Try to pretend like you understand what's important."
"Even your blade knows who will triumph here." —Atraxa, Praetors' Voice
"The Filigree Texts do not compel you to act in accordance with their precepts. They only specify the consequences should you fail." —Lodus of the Ethersworn
Fools surrender their sanity to his riddles. Even greater fools try to solve them.
"It's a fine way to travel, if you don't mind the smell."
Countless delights drift on the surface while dark schemes run below.
"Soaring is wasted on the winged." —Edric, Spymaster of Trest
"To fill your mind with knowledge, we must start by emptying it." —Barrin, master wizard
"The awestruck birds gazed at Wonder. Slowly, timidly, they rose into the air." —*Scroll of Beginnings*
The scrape of shovels and the tumble of cold dirt soon muffled their pleas.
His verdict is always guilty. His sentence is always death.
A single festercreep isn't alone. It's already an infestation.
Grixis is a world where the only things found in abundance are death and decay. Corpses, whole or in part, are the standard currency among necromancers and demons.
"The bonds of loyalty can tie one to the grave." —Crovax, ascendant evincar
Only a thin layer of dirt separates civilization from an undead apocalypse.
Life is such a fragile thing.
The light sigh of its breath whistles through its bones.
"Death is no excuse for disobedience." —Liliana Vess
Little agonies pave the way to greater power.
Necromancers deal in commodities far more precious than gold and grain.
When tempers run high, it's easy to lose your head.
"If fear is the only tool you have left, then you'll never control me." —Xantcha, to Gix
Whether trained, ridden, or eaten, few goblin military innovations have rivaled the bug.
"Holy places are no longer sanctuary from death, and death is no longer sanctuary from anything." —Thalia, Knight-Cathar
Giants share nothing but their fury.
When the moon rises and the bloodlust takes hold, nothing matters but the kill.
Its wings shimmer with dreams absorbed from its enemies.
"It has been my experience that disasters like to strike in pairs."
They fell screaming into the depths of the chasm like so many pebbles tossed down a well.
"Avacyn has abandoned us! We have nothing left except what we can take!"
It is unwise to insult the god of the forge. It is also unwise to stand near anyone else who has insulted him.
"For dim-witted, thick-skulled genetic mutants, they have pretty good aim." —Sisay, captain of the *Weatherlight*
"I wrecked your metal guy, boss. But look! I made you an ashtray."
"If you live on a giant's back, there's only one individual you'll ever need to fear." —Gaddock Teeg
"Oh sure, they buy a lot of ale, but I always find myself needing to rebuild after the giants have paid a visit." —Belko, owner of Titan's Keg tavern
He collects the precious metals, and then converts the rest to propellant.
The knights see a mighty quarry. The dragon sees breakfast, lunch, and dinner.
Nothing breaks the monotony like a good old-fashioned riot.
Elementals are ideas given form. This one is the idea of "smashitude."
Its open mouth is a furnace blast that blisters the skin. Its smoking fists are meteors that split the earth.
"Where will you run when I punish you with the very ground you flee on?" —Nicol Bolas
"Fate is not as fixed as you might think."
"Behold astronomy's contribution to war." —Fennor Rhyl, starcaller
"Where a lesser mind sees junk, I see infinite potential."
Disaster stalks with gaping jaws across unready lands.
Ever since the disaster, the city's survivors viewed the star-strewn sky with dread.
Boggarts constantly strive to outdo each other with the things they bring back to the warren, each hoping the exploit will become as well-known as those of Auntie Grub.
A hundred generations has he mentored, a hundred armies has he crushed beneath his feet, yet only a hundred words has he ever spoken, each more revered than a hundred books.
The power of a waterfall. The fury of an avalanche. The intellect of a gale-force wind.
He cares not for the disasters his storm brings as long as his path ahead is clear.
Remade by Eldrazi magic, Tuktuk inspired an entire clan of misguided goblins.
Nothing escapes its gaze—or its breath.
Its wings beat to the howls of war and fan the fires of rage.
"Listen to the roar! Feel the thunder! The Immersturm shouts its approval with every bolt of lightning!"
The slag-workers wasted no time in creating their own flare pulses to cleanse the area of the *incompleat*.
"Obey!"
"'I have arrived,' bellowed Brawn, and the plane shuddered." —*Scroll of Beginnings*
All seeds share a common bond, calling to each other across infinity.
She remembers every word spoken, from the hero's oath to the baby's cry.
Its blood is life. Its body is growth.
"Naga shed their scales. We wear ours with pride." —Golran, dragonscale captain
Even baloths fear its feeding time.
"Ach! Hans, run! It's the lhurgoyf!" —Saffi Eriksdotter, last words
There are many ruins, but there used to be many more.
In nature, not a single bone or scrap of flesh goes to waste.
"You may enter, but leave those lifeless things of your world behind." —Modruni, maro-sorcerer
It's no coincidence that the oldest trolls are also the angriest.
One quiet word sets off the stampede.
"Savagery is the birthright of every creature that draws breath—or wishes it could." —Karador, Ghost Chieftain
Some see the world as a place of infinite wonder and knowledge. Some see it as an infinite dinner plate.
Weakness is not in the nature of the Swarm.
Loose earth is not a burial but an appetizer.
The Abzan turn to this spell only as a last resort, for its inevitable result is what they most dread: to be alone.
Only the sun that beats down upon Arashin's walls could shine more brightly.
To protect the alliance between Kjeldor and Yavimaya, they trained in the ways of both.
"Nature is a wonderful engineer but works far too slowly for my tastes."
"Those who are different are untrustworthy, unpredictable. Put your safety in the hands of your own kind." —Bowen, Barrenton guardcaptain
Many who cross Sorin's path come down with a sudden and fatal case of being-in-the-way-of-a-millennia-old-vampire.
"We are all decaying, always in a state of near-death. One moment without breath and we begin to break down." —Cevraya, Golgari shaman
Spitting is the customary greeting between a creature and its magical impostor.
"I used to hurl rocks and eat scraps of meat burned over a fire. Look at what I've become and tell me Simic does not hold infinite possibility."
"When something dies, all things benefit. Well okay, just our things." —Ezoc, Golgari rot farmer
"In case of fire, treachery, citywide riot, political upheaval, or worldwide societal collapse, break glass." —Cluestone inscription
"Have you ever held a Boros signet? There's a weight to it that belies its size—a weight of strength and of pride." —Agrus Kos
Reinforcements . . . or refreshments?
Instead of creating a tool that would be damaged by heat, the Thran built one that was charged by it.
The Phyrexian death machine awoke, its coldsteel heart imbuing it with sinister new power.
It harmonizes with the essence of its master.
"It reflects the purity of Mirrodin-that-was." —Koth of the Hammer
An emblem of a secret guild, the Dimir insignia is seen only by its own members—and the doomed.
Only the Eldrazi mind thinks in the warped paths required to open the hedrons and tap the power within.
"What do you have that I cannot obtain?" —Mairsil, the Pretender
Depending on your point of view, the seal represents a proud guardian of the natural cycle or one who has sold her soul to darkness for eternal life.
"Our glorious infection has taken hold." —Elesh Norn, Grand Cenobite
Most books simply deliver knowledge. This one expects some in return.
Garbage in, treasure out.
After lightning struck the cliffs, the ore became iron, the iron became steel, and the steel became greaves. The lightning never left.
"They'll soon become accustomed to wearing skin that is not their own." —Elesh Norn, Grand Cenobite
Mages come from far and wide to bathe in its wisdom.
"A crafter must imbue her weapon with part of her soul—something the Phyrexians are incapable of doing." —Melira
"What is mana but possibility, an idea not yet given form?" —Jhoira, master artificer
The oil created the mycosynth. The mycosynth created New Phyrexia.
Mephidross gives up treasure easily . . . as long as you take its place.
For the Phyrexians, death is not an end, nor a one-time occurrence.
The form of the sigil is just as important as the sigil itself. If it's carried on a medallion, its bearer is a master. If it's tattooed on the body, its bearer is a slave.
The myr are like the Glimmervoid: blank canvases on which to build grand creations.
The kor send their thopter kites to see if the land is in a welcoming mood.
"Tools and artisans can be destroyed, but the act of creation is inviolate." —Elspeth Tirel
"The shadow travels toward the apex. I predict we will soon see the true measure of darkness."

For the Simic Combine, its sigil serves not as an emblem of honor but as a trademark. Its familiar image on any biological commodity attests to superb craftsmanship, ingenious innovation, and higher cost.
Lost to time is the artificer's art of trapping light from a distant star in a ring of purest gold.
"I have attuned the staff to your screams so that only I may benefit from your pain." —Volux, disciple of Nin
"There is great wisdom in rushing headlong into combat . . . if you're prepared." —Kenjek, captain of the Thousand Swords
Infinite possibilities contained in a finite space.
Its collapse is like the lashing out of a long-dead civilization that resents being forgotten.
"Stop thinking like an artificer, Urza, and start thinking like a father!" —Rayne, chancellor of the Tolarian Academy
It is the forest beyond the horizon, the mountain waiting to be climbed, the new land across the endless sea.
Even a fragment of a powerstone contains within it not just energy, but space—vast dimensions trapped in fragile crystal.
The arbiter Galanda Feudkiller judges Lorwyn's squabbles from a lofty perspective.
"We must rely on our own knowledge, not on the dogma of the seekers or the mutterings of the sphinxes." —Tullus of Palandius
It promises protection to those in need and proclaims a warning to any who would threaten Ravnican law.
History has buried its treasures deep.
When defeat is near and guidance is scarce, all eyes look in one direction.
Structures built from darksteel yield to neither assault nor age.
Murky Otarian tides hide the forgotten treacheries of the Phyrexian war.
Without the interfering hands of civilization, nature will always shape itself to its own needs.
"It was a strange morning. When we awoke, we found our trees transformed. We didn't know whether to water them or polish them." —Pulan, Bant orchardist
Deserted, but not uninhabited.
Kuldotha, wellspring of molten metal, temple of the goblin horde.
The dense jungle surrenders to a lush and lavish expanse. At its center uncoil the spires of Qarsi Palace.
"So even the heart of our world has succumbed." —Koth of the Hammer
Once guarded by the Knights of the Reliquary, the tower stands now protected only by its own remoteness, its dusty treasures open to plunder by anyone.
That which endures, survives.
For wisdom's sake, it was built high to gaze on all things. For glory's sake, it was built high as a testament of power. For strength's sake, it was built high to repel all attacks.
On Otaria, peace and harmony are rare. Places that provide both are cherished.
Those who bring nothing to the temple take nothing away.
"When gods become apathetic, the people will worship anyone who answers their pleas." —Kiora
Take two steps north into the unsettled future, south into the unquiet past, east into the present day, or west into the great unknown.
